parsed.main_gap: Step 2 uses the false principle that a non-increasing positive integer starting above 1 cannot reach 1; survival of a nonunit needs a separate one-line argument.

errors.description: The stated inference is false: a non-increasing positive integer may decrease to 1. The needed conclusion is easily repaired by observing that every legal replacement produces at least one entry greater than 1.
errors.quote: A positive integer that never increases and starts above $1$ can never reach $1$; hence $P > 1$ after any number of moves.

errors.description: The final characterization is inaccurate for primes absent from every initial number: any positive proposed exponent divides all the zero valuations, so the stated divisibility condition does not determine a unique maximal integer without an additional support restriction.
errors.quote: the unique maximal $d$ with $v_p(d) \mid v_p(a_i)$ for all $p$ and all $i$.

parsed.notes: Termination and the prime-wise valuation invariant are correct and establish choice-independence. The sole gap in the main proof is local and straightforwardly repairable; the boxed formula is correct.
